Training

In-house courses built on your own services, contracts and tools. Each course mixes concepts, calculations and workshops; participants leave with deliverables they can use the next day.

In-house
6 to 12 participants from the same organisation, working on your real cases.
On site or remote
On site in the Paris region, or remote in half-day sessions.
Three languages
In French, English or Arabic; materials in French or English.
Tailored
Programme adjusted after a scoping interview; courses can be combined into tracks.

Assessment

Placement questionnaire before the course, knowledge assessment at the end, certificate of attendance. Workshop deliverables are reviewed by the trainer.

These courses do not prepare for official certification exams (ITIL, ISO, FinOps): they focus on putting things into practice.

Cloud & hybrid architecture

Designing a target platform, deciding where each workload belongs, and scaling it without losing control of costs.

Duration
3 days
Audience
Architects, infrastructure and operations managers, tech leads.
Prerequisites
Infrastructure basics (network, storage, virtualisation).
Frameworks
  • AWS Well-Architected
  • Azure Well-Architected
  • ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018
  • SecNumCloud

Objectives

  • Choose between IaaS, CaaS, PaaS and SaaS, and between public, private and hybrid cloud, using explicit criteria.
  • Design a landing zone: accounts, network, identity, security, observability.
  • Calculate the availability of an architecture and match it to the target commitments.
  • Build a realistic, costed migration roadmap.

Programme

Day 1 · Scope and choose

  • Service and deployment models, shared responsibility
  • Workload placement criteria: criticality, data, latency, cost, reversibility, sovereignty
  • Landing zones: account structure, hub-and-spoke network, identity, guardrails

Day 2 · Resilience and scalability

  • Zones and regions, active-active and active-passive redundancy
  • Composite availability: links in series and in parallel
  • Capacity tiers, load testing, horizontal and vertical scaling
  • Backup, replication, RTO and RPO per service

Day 3 · Migrate and control

  • Migration strategies (rehost, replatform, refactor, retire…) and wave planning
  • Infrastructure as code and environment automation
  • First FinOps levers: allocation, rightsizing, usage commitments
  • Architecture governance: principles, decision records, reviews

Hands-on work

  • Placement matrix of your applications across service models
  • Availability calculation for your current and target architecture
  • Outline of a wave-based migration roadmap

What you take away

  • Placement decision grid
  • Architecture document template
  • Composite availability calculator

Resilience & compliance: DORA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001

Linking regulatory requirements to architecture and operations, so you hold up when a link fails and can prove it.

Duration
3 days
Audience
Business continuity managers, CISOs and risk teams, operations managers, architects.
Prerequisites
Knowledge of your IT organisation and main suppliers.
Frameworks
  • DORA (EU Regulation 2022/2554)
  • ISO 22301
  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022
  • ISO/IEC 20000-1
  • BSI IT-Grundschutz

Objectives

  • Understand the five pillars of DORA and what they concretely require from IT teams.
  • Run a business impact analysis and set RTO, RPO and maximum tolerable downtime.
  • Connect BCP, DRP, incident management and resilience testing.
  • Map DORA, ISO 22301 and ISO 27001 together to avoid running three projects in parallel.

Programme

Day 1 · DORA

  • Scope and timeline, role of the supervisory authorities
  • ICT risk management: framework, mapping, critical or important functions
  • ICT-related incidents: classification, major incidents, reporting
  • Digital operational resilience testing, including threat-led penetration testing
  • ICT third-party risk: contractual clauses, register of information, exit strategies

Day 2 · Business continuity (ISO 22301)

  • Business continuity management system: context, leadership, improvement
  • Business impact analysis and risk assessment
  • Continuity strategies, BCP and DRP, crisis team
  • Exercises: tabletop, live failover, lessons learned

Day 3 · Security and alignment

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022: ISMS and Annex A controls
  • Cloud extensions: ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018
  • Link with service management (ISO/IEC 20000-1) and service levels
  • Cross-compliance matrix and audit preparation

Hands-on work

  • Impact analysis of one of your critical services
  • Review of a supplier contract against DORA
  • Crisis exercise scenario and evaluation grid

What you take away

  • DORA / ISO 22301 / ISO 27001 mapping matrix
  • BIA and DRP sheet templates
  • Supplier contract clause checklist

SRE & SLOs

Measuring reliability from the user's point of view, setting objectives and steering trade-offs with the error budget.

Duration
2 days
Audience
Run and SRE teams, product owners, operations managers.
Prerequisites
Hands-on use of a monitoring tool (Prometheus, Dynatrace, Zabbix, Centreon or similar).
Frameworks
  • Google SRE
  • OpenSLO
  • ITIL 4

Objectives

  • Choose SLIs that reflect the user experience: availability, latency, quality, freshness.
  • Set SLOs and an error budget policy agreed by product and operations.
  • Implement alerts based on error budget burn rate.
  • Run blameless post-mortems and reduce toil.

Programme

Day 1 · Measure

  • Perceived reliability versus component reliability
  • Types of SLIs and calculation methods: requests, windows, probes
  • Setting an SLO: history, user expectations, cost of each extra nine
  • Error budget and its policy: release freezes, prioritisation

Day 2 · Steer

  • Multi-window burn-rate alerting
  • Major incident management: roles, communication, restoration
  • Post-mortems, corrective actions, follow-up
  • Measuring toil and automating it away

Hands-on work

  • SLIs and SLOs for two of your services
  • Burn-rate alerts configured in your monitoring tool
  • A post-mortem written from a real incident

What you take away

  • SLO sheets for your services
  • Error budget policy
  • Post-mortem template

Service Level Management: SLAs, OLAs and UCs

Writing achievable service commitments, from the customer contract down to internal teams and suppliers.

Duration
2 days
Audience
Service managers, IT contract and procurement managers, architects, operations managers.
Prerequisites
None; basic ITIL knowledge helps.
Frameworks
  • ITIL 4: service level management
  • ISO/IEC 20000-1
  • DORA: third parties

Objectives

  • Build the SLI → SLO → OLA → UC → SLA chain and explain every calculation in it.
  • Write a complete SLA: scope, service hours, measurements, exclusions, credits and penalties.
  • Align internal teams' OLAs and suppliers' UCs with the SLA.
  • Run data-driven service reviews.

Programme

Day 1 · Design the chain

  • Service catalogue and commitment tiers
  • Anatomy of an SLA, an OLA and an underpinning contract
  • Calculations: error budget, SLO margin, links in series and in parallel, maintenance windows
  • Market SLA benchmark: cloud providers, banking sector

Day 2 · Formalise and govern

  • SLA / OLA / UC traceability and RACI matrices
  • Service credits and penalties: calculation, caps, side effects
  • Auditable calculation methods and measurement sources
  • Monthly service review, reporting and continuous improvement

Hands-on work

  • Breaking a real SLA down into OLAs and UCs
  • Writing an SLA sheet and its OLA sheets
  • Simulated service review with credits

What you take away

  • SLA, OLA and UC sheet templates
  • Traceability matrix
  • Commitment chain calculator

Operational excellence: ITIL 4 and ISO/IEC 20000

Organising service practices around the value they create, then measuring their progress.

Duration
2 days
Audience
Operations managers, service managers, support and Run teams.
Prerequisites
None.
Frameworks
  • ITIL 4 (and earlier versions v2 and v3)
  • ISO/IEC 20000-1
  • DORA DevOps metrics

Objectives

  • Position ITIL 4: service value system, value chain, four dimensions.
  • Improve key practices: incidents, problems, changes, service levels.
  • Understand the requirements of an ISO/IEC 20000-1 service management system.
  • Measure and steer continuous improvement.

Programme

Day 1 · Practices

  • What changed between ITIL v2, v3 and 4
  • Incident and problem management, major incidents
  • Change enablement: risk, approval, automation
  • Service level and supplier management

Day 2 · System and measurement

  • ISO/IEC 20000-1 requirements and audit preparation
  • Metrics: lead times, quality, satisfaction, DORA DevOps metrics
  • Continual improvement register and PDCA cycle
  • Maturity roadmap

Hands-on work

  • Maturity assessment of your practices
  • Redesign of a change process
  • Continuous improvement dashboard

What you take away

  • Maturity grid
  • Continual improvement register
  • 12-month roadmap

FinOps

Making cloud cost visible, shared and arbitrable between finance, product and engineering.

Duration
1 day
Audience
Infrastructure managers, architects, IT controllers, product owners.
Prerequisites
Use of at least one public or private cloud.
Frameworks
  • FinOps Framework (FinOps Foundation)

Objectives

  • Understand the inform, optimise and operate phases.
  • Set up cost allocation: tagging, showback, chargeback.
  • Identify savings levers: rightsizing, usage commitments, removing idle resources.
  • Arbitrate between cost, performance and availability.

Programme

Morning · See

  • FinOps principles and roles
  • Cost allocation and tagging strategy
  • Unit cost per service, customer or transaction

Afternoon · Act

  • Optimisation levers and priorities
  • Usage commitments and reservations
  • The cost of availability: what one more nine costs
  • Governance, budgets and alerts

Hands-on work

  • Analysis of a real cloud bill and a prioritised savings plan

What you take away

  • Tagging policy
  • Costed optimisation plan

DevOps & Platform Engineering

Delivering more often and more safely, with an internal platform run as a product.

Duration
2 days
Audience
Platform and DevOps teams, developers, engineering managers.
Prerequisites
CI/CD and container basics.
Frameworks
  • DORA DevOps metrics
  • Team Topologies
  • CNCF Platforms White Paper

Objectives

  • Measure delivery performance with the DORA DevOps metrics.
  • Design a self-service internal platform and its golden paths.
  • Automate infrastructure and security controls in the delivery pipeline.
  • Organise teams around flow.

Programme

Day 1 · Deliver

  • Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore
  • CI/CD pipeline, progressive delivery strategies
  • Infrastructure as code, policy as code

Day 2 · Platform

  • Platform as a product: users, roadmap, adoption
  • Developer portal, service catalogue, golden paths
  • Team topologies and cognitive load
  • Platform reliability: internal SLOs

Hands-on work

  • Measuring your DORA DevOps metrics
  • Designing a golden path for one type of application

What you take away

  • DORA DevOps dashboard
  • Platform roadmap

AI in IT operations

Automating collection, detection, drafting and reporting with AI agents, without losing control.

Duration
1 day, plus an optional workshop day
Audience
IT and operations leaders, architects, Run teams, compliance.
Prerequisites
No technical prerequisites for the first day.
Frameworks
  • EU AI Act
  • ISO/IEC 42001
  • agent-constitution (open source)

Objectives

  • Identify the AI use cases that deliver a measurable gain in operations.
  • Understand the limits of language models and where deterministic code belongs.
  • Define guardrails: scope of action, human sign-off, traceability.
  • Position your use cases within the EU AI Act.

Programme

Morning · Understand

  • Overview of use cases: monitoring, incidents, compliance, reporting, documentation
  • AI agents: tools, autonomy, risks
  • Why calculations stay in code and decisions stay with people

Afternoon · Govern

  • EU AI Act: risk categories and obligations by role
  • Agent charter, logging, human review
  • Demonstration: the service level chain automated end to end

Optional day · Build

  • Prototype on one of your processes: collection, calculation, detection, drafting
  • Measuring the gain and planning the rollout

Hands-on work

  • Mapping and prioritising the automatable tasks of your team

What you take away

  • AI agent usage charter
  • Automation roadmap
